TOP OF BOOK

  • ING GROEP (INGA/ING) [DELTA ▲] — Q2 beat + guidance upgrade drop today; stock +3.5% premarket, approaching 52-week high.
    • Vs. baseline: ING beat on both EPS ($0.78 vs. $0.74 est.) and revenue ($7.17bn vs. $7.06bn est.), then raised full-year guidance. Total income now expected to exceed €24.5bn in 2026 and €26bn in 2027 — the 2027 target is a meaningful step-up. Fee income hit €5bn in 2026, one year ahead of the original Capital Markets Day plan.
    • Read: Total income +10% YoY, supported by +10.7% commercial NII and +14% fee income; ROTE 17% in Q2. Positive operating jaws — income +5% over 12 months while headcount fell 1% and costs rose only 2%. The fee-income acceleration ahead of schedule de-risks the NII sensitivity story. CET1 improved to 13.1% — lean but distributions confirmed. Leg: equity bullish. Any residual short thesis on NIM compression is losing ground. Action: add / hold long.
    • Sources: Investing.com transcript | Quartr summary
  • UniCredit (UCG) / Commerzbank (CBK) [DELTA ▲] — Commerzbank supervisory board formally opens takeover talks; deal path materially de-risked.
    • Vs. baseline: A week ago Orcel guided to a Q4 closing and signalled concessions to Berlin. The break: after months of firm opposition, Commerzbank signalled willingness to engage in formal discussions; supervisory board chairman Jens Weidmann announced the change on July 24, acknowledging that UniCredit's shareholding now approaching 48% has fundamentally altered the balance of power. The German Finance Ministry stated it was "now up to the two banks to talk to each other," marking a reversal of government opposition, while noting ongoing concern about the "aggressive approach."
    • Read: This removes the largest residual binary — outright Commerzbank resistance underwritten by Berlin. UCG's Q2 numbers confirm the deal rationale: record Q2 and H1 net profit of €2.9bn/€6.3bn, 22nd consecutive record quarter. FY26 net profit ambition upgraded to ~€11.5bn (ex-integration costs). Capital sting: year-end CET1 expected ~15% pre-Commerzbank consolidation, ~13% pro-forma for consolidation and buyback cancellation — manageable but capital return paused for CBK holders. Equity leg: UCG long and CBK long (arb compression). Credit leg: CBK senior spreads should grind tighter on reduced uncertainty; pro-forma CET1 compression to ~13% bears monitoring for AT1 headroom. Key remaining risk: regulatory approvals and final price negotiation. Action: hold/add UCG long; dig in on CBK arb spread.
    • Sources: CrowdFund Insider | Bloomberg | UniCredit IR

BY NAME / THEME — PRIMARY (EU)

  • Deutsche Bank (DBK) [DELTA ▲] — Record H1 profit; first-ever buyback from current-year earnings; NII guidance raised.
    • Vs. baseline: DBK reported H1 revenue of €17.2bn and post-tax profit of €4.1bn — described as the best half-year profit in the bank's history. New item: a new €500m buyback from current-year net income, the first time the bank has initiated a buyback funded from current-year earnings. IB led with highest-ever Q2 revenues; IBCM EMEA market share up 40bps to 4.1%. Full-year NII guidance raised to slightly above €14bn. CET1 at 13.9%; MDA buffer 270bps.
    • Read: The earnings-funded buyback is a quality signal — management confident enough in forward generation to not wait for year-end audit. Revenue streak now 20 consecutive quarters; CRE de-risking progressing but portfolio described as resilient. EPS missed on reported basis despite revenue beat — watch tax line for re-ratings. NII guidance raised to slightly above €14bn supports net interest income visibility into H2. Leg: equity constructive, senior non-preferred spreads should be stable/slight tightening bias. Action: hold long.
    • Sources: Deutsche Bank IR | Yahoo Finance
  • UBS (UBSG) [IN LINE] — Q2 beat on revenue ($13.7bn, +13%), slight EPS miss; $3bn buyback confirmed; CS integration near complete.
    • Vs. baseline: EPS $0.87, missed est. by $0.10; revenue $13.7bn beat est. by $580m. $12.6bn of $13.5bn gross cost savings realised — 93% done. CET1 14.4%, above 14% guidance. Equities trading +53% YoY to >$2.3bn for second consecutive quarter. Wealth NNA of $35.5bn in Q2; AuM a record $4.94tn.
    • Read: The EPS miss is PPA/integration noise; operating momentum is strong. The Swiss parliament capital rules debate (full CET1 backing for foreign subs, 7-year transition) remains the structural overhang — the requirement to back foreign units fully with CET1 has been maintained, though software/DTA treatment was softened. Any parliamentary dilution of the foreign-sub rule would be a material positive re-rating catalyst for the equity, as it would release CET1 currently held against foreign subsidiaries, improving capital fungibility and distributions. Major shareholder announcement per GlobeNewswire today — likely a routine >5% threshold filing; verify before acting. Leg: equity constructive; Swiss capital rules are the swing factor for CET1 and distribution capacity. Action: monitor Swiss parliamentary debate on banking bill; hold.
    • Sources: TipRanks | Swiss Federal Council
  • Barclays (BARC/BCS) [DELTA ▲] — Income target lifted to ~£31.5bn; IB equities +44%, advisory +51%; EPS miss is optics not operations.
    • Vs. baseline: Q2 income £8.3bn, PBT +30% to £3.3bn, group RoTE 16.1%; 2026 income target raised to ~£31.5bn. £1bn buyback and £800m interim dividend announced; H1 distributions £2.3bn (+61% YoY). CET1 stable at 14.3% (14.0% pro-forma for buyback). EPS $0.23 vs. $0.82 est. — a 72% miss in percentage terms; driven by US securitised loan margin compression, not operational failure.
    • Read: The EPS miss is a US consumer banking mechanics issue — higher benchmark rates compressed margins on securitised loans, reducing NII contribution from that book; quarterly income may not fully build back to the Q1 level during 2026. UK businesses all >20% RoTE; IB performing strongly. The stock's -6% premarket reaction on results day already partially reversed given the revenue beat and guidance upgrade. Loan loss rate guided near top of 50-60bps range — not ringing any alarm. Leg: equity now looks oversold on EPS headline vs. underlying beat; credit constructive. Action: add on dip if share weakness persists.
    • Sources: LiveSquawk | Yahoo Finance
  • Santander (SAN) [IN LINE] — H1 underlying profit +15% to €7.3bn; TSB acquisition closed April 30; 2026 targets reaffirmed.
    • Vs. baseline: Q2 underlying net profit €3.77bn (+17%), marginally above €3.75bn forecast; attributable profit +3% to €3.52bn after €250m TSB restructuring costs; higher impairments in Argentina and Brazil partial offset. TSB acquisition strengthens UK franchise with £400m+ expected cost synergies. ~€1.8bn H1'26 buyback already approved by ECB.
    • Read: Broadly in line; the print is now resolved. LatAm credit provisioning bears watching — Argentina and Brazil are the margin of risk for H2; elevated provisions would compress group NII and widen cost-of-risk guidance. UK NII tailwind from higher rates partly offset by TSB integration costs. Net-net: no new information for a thesis change. Action: no action / monitor LatAm provisions.
    • Sources: Santander IR
  • Julius Baer (BAER) [DELTA ▲] — Record H1 net profit CHF 673m, +128% YoY; AuM at all-time high CHF 547bn.
    • Vs. baseline: IFRS net profit rose to record CHF 673m (EPS CHF 3.27), up 128% from CHF 295m in H1 2025 (when hit by loan-loss provisions); adjusted net profit up 32% on underlying basis. Record net profit driven by pronounced client activity, all-time high AuM, net new money inflows, and improved operating leverage.
    • Read: The year-ago comp was depressed by Signa/private credit provisions; +32% on an underlying basis is the cleaner number. The turnaround under CEO Bollinger is executing well; net new money inflows and AuM at record levels are positive flow data points for sector. Fee income sensitivity to AuM levels means continued inflows directly support recurring revenue; FX moves in CHF/EUR remain a headwind to watch on AuM translation. Equity long re-rating thesis has substance if mid-term targets hold. Action: hold/add.
    • Sources: EQS/Julius Baer
  • Private Credit — Ares / Europe Direct Lending [NEW] — Ares preparing €3bn credit secondaries sale from flagship Ares Capital Europe IV; one of the largest ever.
    • Vs. baseline: Ares is preparing to sell €3bn ($3.4bn) of bundled LP stakes in Ares Capital Europe IV via a credit secondaries process — one of the largest credit-secondaries deals ever; in talks with credit-secondaries investors.
    • Read: This is a GP liquidity management/portfolio rotation event, not a distress signal. But it arrives alongside a key thematic data point: European direct lenders face slowing deal flow from weak M&A and software-sector pullback; the US faces a $14bn redemption backlog pressuring managers to limit new commitments. A successful close at a tight secondary discount would be mark-to-market supportive for other European direct-lending funds and their NAV-based fee income. A wide discount would pressure NAV marks industry-wide, compressing management fees and triggering potential covenant reviews on NAV-linked credit facilities. Monitor pricing and discount vs. par. US BDC spread implications if the discount sets a new clearing level. Action: dig in — get pricing details when deal closes.
    • Sources: Bloomberg | Yahoo Finance / Bloomberg
  • European Direct Lending — Spreads / Software Sector [DELTA ▼] — Software de-rated as collateral; deal flow compressed; but competition intense for remaining buyouts.
    • Vs. baseline: Software has fallen out of favour as collateral as AI-driven disruption to business models is reassessed; "some lenders were considering those assets as risk-free, but they're not" (Allianz GI CIO); deal flow has slowed and exposure is being capped at ~5%. Recent cleared deal: CVC, Goldman Sachs and Apollo provided a €425m loan to GBA Group at ~E+475bps.
    • Read: E+475bps for a BB-ish lab-services credit is consistent with recent European direct-lending spread widening. If software exposure is being capped at 5% industry-wide, secondary marks on portfolios heavy in software names face pressure, with direct NII impact on BDCs and direct-lending funds carrying floating-rate software loans at compressed recoverable values. Read-through to bank syndication pipelines: fewer large-cap software LBOs means weaker leveraged-finance fee income in H2. Action: monitor; dig in on private credit fund NAV marks when available.
    • Sources: Yahoo Finance

CREDIT CORNER

  • HSBC (HSBA) [NEW] — H1 2026 results due 4 August; EPS consensus $2.24 vs. $2.12 Q1 actual.
    • Read: HSBC will announce Interim 2026 Results on 4 August at 5am BST. Asia-Pacific macro and Hong Kong property exposure are the key risks given elevated geopolitical tension in the region; any deterioration in Asian NII or wealth fee income would weigh on senior and AT1 spreads. With peers (DBK, UBS, Barclays) all beating on IB and wealth, any HSBC miss on wealth or Asian NII will be idiosyncratic, not sector. Leg: equity and senior. Action: positioned for binary — watch AML/conduct any residual headline risk. Monitor.
    • Sources: HSBC IR
  • BNP Paribas (BNP) [IN LINE] — Q2 results reported 23 July; CET1 already at 13% — 2027 target met early; SRT usage active.
    • Read: BNP has already met its CET1 ratio objective of 13% set for 2027. SRT and credit insurance actively used for RWA savings — cumulative €63bn of RWA savings equating to ~90bps of CET1. CET1 ahead of target is a distribution optionality signal; excess capital above the 13% floor provides headroom for buybacks or AT1 calls without pressuring funding spreads. BNP is the most active European bank SRT issuer — watch for new SRT/CLO pipeline in H2 as they maintain capital efficiency. Credit leg: senior non-preferred tight; AT1s constructive. Action: monitor for SRT pipeline news.
    • Sources: BNP Paribas IR

SECONDARY — US / MACRO READ-THROUGH

  • US Fed / FOMC (July 29 meeting) [IN LINE] — Hold 3.50–3.75% for fifth consecutive meeting; three dissents for +25bps; September hike probability ~60%.
    • Vs. baseline: Fed held at 3.50–3.75% as expected; three FOMC members dissented in favour of a +25bps hike — the largest dissent bloc this cycle — leaving the door open to September. Post-presser September hike probability at 60.1% per CME FedWatch.
    • Read: Three dissents is a hawkish signal even in a hold — this is not a clean pass. Core PCE June: +3.3% YoY (in line with forecast), +0.1% MoM — a monthly undershoot vs. +0.2% estimate. The soft monthly print provides cover for September patience, but if July energy prices reverse (Brent has been oscillating $87–$93), the September decision is live. Transmission to European financials: (1) higher UST yields support EUR rate-stay narrative and ECB September hawkishness, sustaining NII tailwinds for EU banks; (2) USD funding cost remains elevated for EU banks' US dollar books, compressing spread on USD-denominated assets; (3) widening US IG/HY spreads (if September hike materialises) would be a read-through on EU credit and leveraged-finance pipeline. Action: monitor September path carefully; hedge rate exposure if Brent re-spikes.
    • Sources: Trading Economics | Schwab | Advisor Perspectives / BEA
